metadataReview.note: The engagement is located at the township of Mạo Khê in present Quảng Ninh province, whose French post the Uông Bí municipal history names as a target of the 1951 Hoàng Hoa Thám campaign and which the French Ministry of the Armed Forces names among de Lattre’s victories in Tonkin. The point is a township reference, not the separate outpost, mine or church positions. The existing dates are retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred from these sources.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: GeoNames feature 1574873, Thị Trấn Mạo Khê (populated place, Đông Triều, Quảng Ninh), publishes latitude 21.05858 and longitude 106.59255, rounded to [106.5926,21.0586]. This is a township-scale sector reference: the Wikipedia pointer describes surrounding outposts, a coal-mine position about 1 km north and a fortified church east of the town, none of which is located individually. It is not a surveyed post, a unit position or the extent of the engagement. The much larger present Mạo Khê ward and its movable map label are not used, and no accuracy radius is claimed.
